name: Chattoko
author: chattoko

sections.description:
Chattoko adds a live chat widget to your WordPress site, backed by an AI assistant that you teach with your own FAQs and documents. It answers the questions you get every day, and when a question needs a person, it hands over cleanly — with the whole conversation already in front of your agent.

This plugin is the connector between your WordPress site and your Chattoko account. A Chattoko account is required — the chat itself runs on the Chattoko service.

What you get

  • An AI assistant trained on your own FAQs, documents and website content
  • Live chat with real-time typing indicators, then a clean handoff to a human agent
  • Proactive messages and chat flows — greet visitors, ask qualifying questions, capture leads
  • A shared inbox for your team, with tickets and email in the same place
  • Visitor context: which page they are on, device, approximate location
  • Customer satisfaction surveys after a chat
  • Available in 10 languages

Plans and trial

Every plan starts with a 14-day free trial. Chat plans start at US$59 a month; plans with phone calls and SMS start at US$139 a month. See https://chattoko.io for current pricing. The plugin itself is free and has no locked features: everything you pay for runs on the Chattoko service.

WooCommerce

If WooCommerce is active, the plugin reports the visitor’s cart value, currency and item count to the widget. That lets your chat flows react to the cart — for example, offer help when a cart passes a value you choose, or greet someone who has just added an item. You can turn this off in the plugin settings.

The cart is read in the visitor’s browser from WooCommerce’s own Store API (/wp-json/wc/store/v1/cart), and read again when an item is added, so AJAX add-to-cart works without a page reload. Nothing visitor-specific is printed into your pages, so page caching stays safe.

Separately, you can connect your store in the Chattoko dashboard (Integrations → WooCommerce, with a read-only REST API key). The AI can then look up a customer’s orders and answer questions about your products.

Setup

  1. Install and activate the plugin
  2. Paste your Workspace ID from your Chattoko dashboard
  3. Save — the widget appears on your site

External services

This plugin connects your site to Chattoko, a hosted live chat service operated by Chattoko (https://chattoko.io). The plugin is a connector; the chat service itself runs on Chattoko’s servers, and a Chattoko account is required to use it.

What the plugin loads

Once you save a Workspace ID, the plugin loads the chat widget script from https://chattoko.io/widget/widget.js on your site’s front end, and adds the Workspace ID to your pages as a <meta name="chattoko-workspace"> tag so the widget can find it. Before a Workspace ID is saved, the plugin loads nothing and contacts no external server.

Which servers the widget talks to

Chattoko’s backend runs on Google Cloud, so once the widget is running in a visitor’s browser it contacts these hosts directly. They are all part of the Chattoko service:

  • chattoko.io — the widget script itself, and anonymous counts of how visitors use the chat button and greeting: shown, opened or dismissed (chattoko.io/w/ev)
  • identitytoolkit.googleapis.com and securetoken.googleapis.com — Firebase Authentication, used to give the visitor an anonymous identity so their conversation can be theirs alone. The second host renews that identity when a visitor comes back later
  • firestore.googleapis.com — Firebase Firestore, the live database that carries the conversation between the visitor and your agents
  • firebasestorage.googleapis.com — Firebase Storage: your business logo in the chat window on every page where the widget loads, and any file or image attached to a chat
  • australia-southeast1-chat-app-b5947.cloudfunctions.net — Chattoko’s backend functions on Google Cloud Functions, contacted only when a visitor asks for a copy of the conversation by email, confirms their phone number with a code, or opens a link that continues a conversation started by text message
  • www.google.com, www.gstatic.com and content-firebaseappcheck.googleapis.com — Google reCAPTCHA Enterprise and Firebase App Check, which protect the chat from automated abuse. reCAPTCHA looks at how the page is used in the visitor’s browser and sends that to Google to tell people from bots. Its use is subject to the Google Privacy Policy (https://policies.google.com/privacy) and Terms of Service (https://policies.google.com/terms)
  • fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com — Google Fonts, for the widget’s typeface

Google Fonts and reCAPTCHA both run in the visitor’s browser and reach Google directly, so the visitor’s IP address reaches Google. Some jurisdictions treat that as needing consent. If that applies to you, take it into account before enabling the widget.

What is sent to Chattoko, and when

The widget runs in your visitors’ browsers and sends data to Chattoko’s servers:

  • On every page where the widget loads: the page URL and title, referrer, browser and device type, language, and an approximate location derived from the visitor’s IP address. A first-party identifier is stored in the browser so a returning visitor’s conversation continues.
  • When a visitor opens the chat and writes: their messages, and any name, email address or phone number they choose to provide.
  • If the WooCommerce option is enabled: the value of the items in the cart (with tax and discounts, without shipping), the currency and the number of items, read from your own store’s Store API in the visitor’s browser and passed to the widget when a page loads and when the cart changes.

This data is processed by Chattoko to deliver the chat service — showing the conversation to your agents, generating AI replies, and producing your analytics.

Terms and privacy

  • Terms of Service: https://chattoko.io/terms
  • Privacy Policy: https://chattoko.io/privacy

Because the widget collects visitor data, review your own site’s privacy policy and any consent requirements that apply to you before enabling it.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin through Plugins → Add New, or upload the chattoko folder to /wp-content/plugins/
  2. Activate it through the Plugins menu
  3. Go to Settings → Chattoko
  4. Paste your Workspace ID and save

You will find your Workspace ID in the Chattoko dashboard under Settings → Installation. No account yet? Sign up at https://chattoko.io/signup and start a 14-day free trial.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Chattoko account?

Yes. This plugin connects your WordPress site to the Chattoko service — the chat, the AI and your team inbox all live there. You can create an account at https://chattoko.io/signup.

Where do I find my Workspace ID?

Log in to your Chattoko dashboard, go to Settings → Installation, and copy the ID under Your workspace ID. It is 6 to 64 letters, numbers, dashes or underscores. If you paste something else, the plugin keeps the ID you had and tells you why.

How much does Chattoko cost?

Every plan starts with a 14-day free trial. Chat plans start at US$59 a month, and plans with phone calls and SMS at US$139 a month. Current prices are on https://chattoko.io.

Does the widget slow my site down?

The widget script is loaded with defer, so it never blocks your page from rendering. It is served from a CDN and loads after your content.

Does it work with WooCommerce?

Yes. When WooCommerce is active, the plugin reports the cart value, currency and item count so your chat flows can react to what is in the cart. It can be switched off in the plugin settings. Connect the store under Integrations → WooCommerce in your Chattoko dashboard and the AI can also look up orders and products.

Does it work with caching and optimisation plugins?

Yes. Nothing visitor-specific is printed into your pages, so full-page caching is safe. The Workspace ID is also printed as a meta tag, so the chat keeps working when an optimisation plugin combines or delays scripts. We tested Autoptimize and LiteSpeed Cache, including LiteSpeed’s “Combine External and Inline JS”. If you combine scripts, the bundled copy of the widget only updates when your cache is cleared, so excluding chattoko.io/widget from JS combining keeps you on the latest version.

What happens if I deactivate the plugin?

The widget stops loading immediately. Your Workspace ID is kept so you can reactivate without setting it up again — deleting the plugin removes it.

Is my visitors’ data sent to a third party?

Yes — the chat service is hosted by Chattoko. The “External services” section above lists exactly what is sent and when, and links to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.
